b2plus-erweiterte-partizipialattribute.title: Extended Participial Attributes
b2plus-erweiterte-partizipialattribute.pattern: der [modifier(s)] + participle + noun: der schnell laufende Mann; die von allen bewunderte Künstlerin
b2plus-erweiterte-partizipialattribute.explanation: An "extended" participial attribute packs an entire clause's worth of information between the article and the noun, with the participle itself sitting right before the noun: "der schnell laufende Mann" (the man running quickly, from "der Mann, der schnell läuft"), "die von allen bewunderte Künstlerin" (the artist admired by everyone, from "die Künstlerin, die von allen bewundert wird"). This is extremely common in written/journalistic German because it compresses a relative clause into a single noun phrase.
b2plus-erweiterte-partizipialattribute.fact: The reading strategy is to find the participle first (it's always right before the noun, carrying the adjective ending), then read everything between the article and the participle as if it were the missing relative clause's content, mentally reordering it into normal subject-verb order — this trick makes even long, dense extended attributes tractable.

dialogue.native: Wer ist die von allen bewunderte Künstlerin?

dialogue.native: Das ist die vor kurzem ausgezeichnete Malerin aus Dresden.
dialogue.en: That's the recently awarded painter from Dresden.

b2plus-nominalstil.title: Nominal Style vs. Verbal Style
b2plus-nominalstil.pattern: Nominalstil: compact, noun-heavy, formal; Verbalstil: clause-heavy, natural, conversational
b2plus-nominalstil.explanation: German writing sits on a spectrum between "Nominalstil" (nominal style: dense, noun-heavy, favored in bureaucratic, legal, and academic writing) and "Verbalstil" (verbal style: built from clauses and verbs, favored in conversation and narrative). The same content can be expressed either way: "Nach Abschluss der Untersuchung erfolgte die Veröffentlichung der Ergebnisse" (Nominalstil) vs. "Nachdem die Untersuchung abgeschlossen war, wurden die Ergebnisse veröffentlicht" (Verbalstil) — both correct, different register.
b2plus-nominalstil.fact: Being able to convert fluidly between the two is a genuine B2+ skill: reading official documents, contracts, and news requires decoding dense Nominalstil, while sounding natural in conversation requires defaulting back to Verbalstil — native speakers constantly switch between them based on context.

dialogue.native: Nach Beendigung der Sitzung erfolgt die Bekanntgabe der Ergebnisse.
dialogue.en: Following the conclusion of the meeting, the results will be announced.

dialogue.native: Das heißt einfach: Wenn die Sitzung endet, werden die Ergebnisse bekannt gegeben.
dialogue.en: That simply means: When the meeting ends, the results will be announced.

b2plus-genitivpraepositionen.title: Advanced Genitive Prepositions
b2plus-genitivpraepositionen.pattern: aufgrund, angesichts, infolge, innerhalb, außerhalb, anhand, mithilfe + Genitiv
b2plus-genitivpraepositionen.explanation: Beyond wegen/trotz/während/statt, formal and written German uses a wider set of Genitiv prepositions: "aufgrund" (due to, based on: "aufgrund der Umstände"), "angesichts" (in view of: "angesichts der Lage"), "infolge" (as a result of: "infolge des Unfalls"), "innerhalb"/"außerhalb" (within/outside: "innerhalb einer Woche"), "anhand" (on the basis of, using: "anhand der Daten"), "mithilfe" (with the help of: "mithilfe eines Experten").
b2plus-genitivpraepositionen.fact: These prepositions cluster heavily in news, academic, and business writing — recognizing them fluently is often more valuable at this level than producing them from scratch, since they signal exactly the kind of formal, evidence-based reasoning ("based on the data", "in view of the situation") that characterizes higher-register texts.

dialogue.native: Wie habt ihr die Entscheidung getroffen?
dialogue.en: How did you make the decision?

b2plus-wortfeld-wirtschaft.title: Vocabulary Domain: Economy and Business
b2plus-wortfeld-wirtschaft.pattern: die Wirtschaft, das Wachstum, die Inflation, der Wettbewerb, die Investition, der Umsatz
b2plus-wortfeld-wirtschaft.explanation: Economic and business vocabulary appears constantly in news, reports, and professional contexts: "die Wirtschaft" (the economy), "das Wachstum" (growth), "die Inflation" (inflation), "der Wettbewerb" (competition), "die Investition" (investment), "der Umsatz" (revenue/turnover), "die Arbeitslosigkeit" (unemployment). Mastering this domain unlocks a huge share of authentic written German.
b2plus-wortfeld-wirtschaft.fact: Many of these nouns pair with a small set of recurring verbs worth learning together: Wirtschaft wächst/schrumpft (grows/shrinks), Preise steigen/sinken (rise/fall), Investitionen tätigen (make investments) — learning noun+verb collocations, not just isolated words, is what makes vocabulary usable in real sentences.

dialogue.native: Wie entwickelt sich die Wirtschaft dieses Jahr?
dialogue.en: How is the economy developing this year?

dialogue.native: Das Wachstum ist stabil, aber die Inflation bereitet vielen Sorgen.
dialogue.en: Growth is stable, but inflation worries many.

b2plus-wortfeld-politik.title: Vocabulary Domain: Politics and Society
b2plus-wortfeld-politik.pattern: die Regierung, die Wahl, die Gesellschaft, die Demokratie, das Gesetz, die Bevölkerung
b2plus-wortfeld-politik.explanation: Political and social vocabulary is essential for following news and discussing current events: "die Regierung" (the government), "die Wahl" (the election), "die Gesellschaft" (society), "die Demokratie" (democracy), "das Gesetz" (the law), "die Bevölkerung" (the population), "die Menschenrechte" (human rights), "die Gerechtigkeit" (justice).
b2plus-wortfeld-politik.fact: These words appear constantly alongside the Konjunktiv I reported speech and passive constructions already learned — political and news texts are, in fact, the natural home of both those grammar points, so practicing this vocabulary alongside them reinforces everything together.

dialogue.native: Was denkst du über die kommende Wahl?
dialogue.en: What do you think about the upcoming election?

dialogue.native: Ich hoffe, dass sich die Regierung mehr um soziale Gerechtigkeit kümmert.
dialogue.en: I hope the government cares more about social justice.

b2plus-wortfeld-wissenschaft.title: Vocabulary Domain: Science and Technology
b2plus-wortfeld-wissenschaft.pattern: die Forschung, die Entdeckung, das Experiment, die Technologie, die Entwicklung, künstliche Intelligenz
b2plus-wortfeld-wissenschaft.explanation: Scientific and technological vocabulary opens up an enormous share of modern written German: "die Forschung" (research), "die Entdeckung" (discovery), "das Experiment" (experiment), "die Technologie" (technology), "die Entwicklung" (development), "künstliche Intelligenz" (artificial intelligence), "die Erkenntnis" (finding/insight). These words often pair with nominalization and passive constructions already learned, since scientific writing favors both registers heavily.
b2plus-wortfeld-wissenschaft.fact: Notice how many of these nouns are themselves nominalizations of familiar verbs (forschen → Forschung, entdecken → Entdeckung, entwickeln → Entwicklung) — recognizing the verb underneath an unfamiliar scientific noun is often the fastest way to guess its meaning without a dictionary.

dialogue.en: What is your team researching right now?

dialogue.native: Wir untersuchen, wie künstliche Intelligenz die Medizin verändern könnte.
dialogue.en: We're investigating how artificial intelligence could change medicine.

b2plus-funktionsverbgefuege.title: Funktionsverbgefüge: Support-Verb Constructions
b2plus-funktionsverbgefuege.pattern: in Kraft treten, zur Verfügung stellen, Rücksicht nehmen, Anwendung finden, zum Ausdruck bringen
b2plus-funktionsverbgefuege.explanation: "Funktionsverbgefüge" pair a semantically "empty" verb (treten, stellen, nehmen, bringen, finden...) with a noun that carries the real meaning, forming a fixed formal expression: "in Kraft treten" (to take effect, literally "to step into force"), "zur Verfügung stellen" (to make available), "Rücksicht nehmen" (to show consideration). These constructions are everywhere in formal, bureaucratic, and journalistic German, often replacing a plain verb ("gelten" → "in Kraft treten" / "berücksichtigen" → "Rücksicht nehmen").
b2plus-funktionsverbgefuege.fact: These phrases must be learned as fixed units, not built from their parts — the noun inside almost always resists a normal article and takes a specific, memorized case ("Rücksicht nehmen AUF + Akkusativ", "zur Verfügung STELLEN" always with "zur", never "zu der" spelled out). Treat each one as its own vocabulary item.

dialogue.en: When does the new law take effect?

b2plus-abstrakte-substantive.title: Complex Sentences with Abstract Nouns
b2plus-abstrakte-substantive.pattern: combining nominalization, genitive prepositions, and passive/modal structures in dense sentences
b2plus-abstrakte-substantive.explanation: At this level, sentences increasingly combine everything learned so far — nominalization, advanced genitive prepositions, passive constructions, and extended attributes — into single, dense, information-rich sentences typical of high-register writing: "Die aufgrund mangelnder Ressourcen verzögerte Umsetzung der Reform sorgte für erhebliche Kritik" (The implementation of the reform, delayed due to lack of resources, caused considerable criticism). Learning to parse and produce such sentences is the core B2+ skill.
b2plus-abstrakte-substantive.fact: The reading strategy for these dense sentences: find the main verb first (it anchors the sentence), then work outward — identify the subject noun phrase (often itself containing a nominalization and an extended attribute), and treat each genitive/prepositional phrase as a separable chunk of information rather than trying to process the whole sentence linearly.

dialogue.native: Was war der Grund für die Verzögerung?
dialogue.en: What was the reason for the delay?

dialogue.native: Die aufgrund technischer Probleme verzögerte Fertigstellung des Projekts sorgte für Unmut.
dialogue.en: The completion of the project, delayed due to technical problems, caused displeasure.

b2plus-stilregister.title: Register-Shifting: Formal vs. Informal
b2plus-stilregister.pattern: same content, different register: formal/written vs. informal/spoken paraphrase
b2plus-stilregister.explanation: Truly advanced German means being able to say the same thing in different registers depending on context — a formal letter to an authority, a casual chat with a friend, a professional email to a colleague. This isn't new grammar so much as a new skill: choosing vocabulary, sentence structure (Nominalstil vs. Verbalstil), and directness level to match the situation.
b2plus-stilregister.fact: A reliable rule of thumb: formal register favors nominalization, passive voice, Konjunktiv II for politeness, and longer sentences with subordinate clauses; informal register favors short main clauses, modal particles (doch, mal, ja), and the active voice with "man" or a direct "du". Recognizing which signals belong to which register lets you shift deliberately instead of by accident.
